1.45.betting_forecast: 11/10 Earth Shot, 9/4 Velvet Vega, 11/2 Blue Noon, 13/2 Malika, 12/1 Wild Violet, 100/1 Mokata, 200/1 Anthena.
1.45.spotlight_verdict: Oaks/Irish Oaks entry EARTH SHOT kept on for a promising second over 1m at Newbury on her sole 2yo start and, with the step up in trip a positive move, she is taken to get off the mark. The 240,000euros Gosden newcomer Velvet Vega is feared most, while Blue Noon and Malika are open to improvement.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: Tailed off at 250-1 on debut at Southwell (7f, AW) last October; has since left Lawrence Mullaney (remains in same ownership); she would be a shock winner on stable debut.

Backed into 15-2 when promising fourth of 12 on debut at Leicester (7f, good to soft) last September; this 420,000euros sister to useful 1m winner Naepoint is open to improvement and could be in the mix if staying 1m2f.

Kept on for 2l second to even-money stablemate and fellow newcomer at Newbury (1m, soft) last October; this Oaks/Irish Oaks entry is bred to be suited by the step up in trip (dam 1m6f Group 3 winner); leading claims.

20-1 and no match for the front three when fourth of 13 on debut at Kempton (1m, AW) last November; others have achieved more but no surprise if she takes a sizeable step forward today for connections who won this last year.

Lost a lot of ground at the start when tenth of 11, beaten just under 13l, on debut at Yarmouth (1m, good; 125-1) three weeks ago; has since left Robert Eddery (remains in same ownership) and new trainer is in fine form; however, it's likely she remains best watched for now.

240,000euros yearling; first foal; dam French 1m/9.5f winner (including Listed), sister to 1m4f winner Pappini, half-sister to French 7f Listed winner Lucie Manette, is granddaughter of Irish/Yorkshire Oaks winner Petrushka; this Lope De Vega newcomer is in top hands and could be a contender.

First foal; dam 7f AW 2yo winner (RPR 79), half-sister to 2m/2m1f hurdle winner Kilcummin, out of French 9.7f winner; refused to enter stalls and withdrawn from intended debut at Newbury on April 17 (40-1 at the time).

2.20.betting_forecast: 8/11 Poseidon's Warrior, 11/4 My Love Is King, 6/1 Lyneham, 12/1 Archers Bay, 16/1 Ancient Egypt.
2.20.spotlight_verdict: Godolphin colt POSEIDON'S WARRIOR kept on strongly for second over 1m1f in the Listed Feilden Stakes here recently and, with the extra furlong a likely plus, he can provide Charlie Appleby with yet another winner in this race. My Love Is King is a highly likeable prospect for the Gosdens and is second choice ahead of course 2yo maiden winner Lyneham, who should have plenty more to offer this season.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: Won fast-ground novice races at Beverley (7.4f) and Goodwood (1m) last summer on his first two starts; he's better than he showed when 14l seventh of eight in the Group 2 Royal Lodge here in September (1m, good to firm; 16-1) and has Dante/Derby entries but others have more pressing claims.

Ex-Ballydoyle colt who got off the mark in first-time cheekpieces (retained since) on his stable debut in a Wolverhampton novice (9.4f, AW) in December and followed up over this C&D (good) 16 days ago on his first handicap start; could continue to progress but does need another step forward today.
horses.breeding: b c Wootton Bassett - The Tooth Fairy

horses.spotlight_comment: Went close on debut at Doncaster (1m, soft) last September then kept on well to win a 1m maiden here (good) in October; this is a much stiffer test of his credentials but his dam is from a classy family and he's in excellent hands; entered in the Dante and Derby and could be set for big 3yo campaign.

Won last November on sole 2yo start (7f, AW) and reappeared with a near-miss in a hot novice contest at Newbury (1m2f, good) a fortnight ago; this Dante/Derby entry is from a classy family and should continue to progress for his top stable; could have a part to play.
horses.breeding: b c Kingman - Fallen In Love

horses.spotlight_comment: Easy win at Goodwood (1m1f, good) last October on second start and he reappeared with a 1l Listed second here (1m1f, good) 16 days ago, staying on well; the first-time hood could help him settle better and he holds leading claims for top trainer who has won three of the last four runnings.
horses.breeding: b c Sea The Stars - Holy Amaretta

2.55.betting_forecast: 7/2 Fort Rock, 4/1 Lake Como, 9/2 Comic Hero, St Anton, 6/1 Zennor Storm, 8/1 Vincenzo Peruggia, 14/1 Elan D'Or, Objector,
2.55.spotlight_verdict: Having run very creditably in third in a conditions race at Kempton in March, when conceding weight all round, LAKE COMO appeals as being well treated back in a handicap and earns the vote ahead of Objector, who is 2-2 and has won easily on both those AW starts. Fort Rock (third choice) and Zennor Storm also arrive with 2-2 records from the AW, while St Anton was a close third in a C&D handicap recently and is also in calculations.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: Went close in two fast-ground novice races last summer and returned with a novice win at Kempton (7f, AW) in February; 15-8 favourite and denied a clear run when 2l fifth of six on handicap debut at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) four weeks ago; retains potential and is not ruled out but he lost places close home once in the clear at Musselburgh and has to raise his game.
horses.breeding: b g Saxon Warrior - Sense Of Humour

horses.spotlight_comment: Got off the mark at the eighth attempt in Chelmsford nursery (7f, AW) last November on his second AW start, and he again had plenty in hand when following up at Kempton (1m, AW); needs to transfer that improvement back to turf but he did show promise on grass last season; not ruled out.
horses.breeding: b c Without Parole - As Good As Gold

horses.spotlight_comment: Won over 7f on Kempton AW last autumn on his first two starts; those were narrow victories and improvement is needed on this handicap debut if he's to remain unbeaten, but he could have plenty more to offer for his top trainer, especially over this extra furlong.

Ran seven times last year and sole win came in four-runner nursery at Kempton (1m, AW); also effective on turf and gelded since last seen; however, unless he finds improvement he's vulnerable to less-exposed types.

Runner-up on final two of his three 2yo starts (7f/1m, good to soft/good) and improved form on recent seasonal/handicap debut when close third over C&D (good); well regarded and open to further improvement; one to consider.

Won at Beverley (7.4f, good to firm) last July on second start then well beaten in Group 2 at Goodwood (7f, good) later that month; reappeared with close second of six in handicap at Musselburgh (1m, good to soft) four weeks ago but it's likely he needs a much bigger run in this hot contest.
horses.breeding: ch c Lope De Vega - Sliabh Luachra

horses.spotlight_comment: Won on debut at Kempton (7f, AW) last October and followed up there (1m, AW) in December; his opening mark is no gift but it remains to be seen where his limitations lie and he's respected for his top yard on turf debut.

3.30.betting_forecast: 5/2 Bay City Roller, 7/2 Lion's Pride, 9/2 Eydon, 5/1 Santorini Star, 13/2 French Master, 8/1 Sunway, 40/1 Paradias.
3.30.spotlight_verdict: This looks pretty open, with one contributory element being the various questions that hang over all the field. Bay City Roller, for instance, impressed in Germany on his final start last season but that was on soft ground. EYDON and Lion's Pride are therefore preferred given that they had notable 1m4f wins last term on good to firm. French Master (interesting after the gelding operation), Sunway and Santorini Star step back down in trip.[Richard Austen]

horses.spotlight_comment: Sole start on good to firm was his debut win; highly reliable since and progressive too overall, taking his form to the next level when landing Group 1 by 7l at Munich (1m4f, soft; his only win last season) in November when last seen; form chance but that's based on the soft-ground performance.

Had 1m4f wins last season in a Group 3 at Newbury (good to firm) in May and Group 2 in Italy (good; made all for career-best form) in October; tailed off in Hong Kong on final start but has a shout if back to his best.
horses.breeding: b h Olden Times - Moon Mountain

horses.spotlight_comment: Won two 1m6f handicaps last term, latterly in taking style from off the pace at Royal Ascot (good to firm) when blinkered first time; slowly away on both subsequent starts, looking as if he was stretched by 2m in the Group 1 Goodwood Cup on first occasion (creditable) but tailed-off second favourite in the Ebor last time (visored; raced wide and made most); back to 1m4f, with headgear removed and needs overall improvement but the gelding operation may have helped.

7l Listed win over C&D (good to firm) last September; there are also plenty of lesser shows to be considered and, after he was not discredited in Qatar in February, he managed only fourth of six when favourite for Group 3 at Newbury 13 days ago; in the mix on peak efforts.
horses.breeding: b g Roaring Lion - Crimson Ribbon

horses.spotlight_comment: In the form of his life this winter with a win at Lingfield (1m4f) in February and close calls in his other three outings; those were on AW, which does seem to suit him particularly well, and also in handicaps, which leaves him with something to find in his first Group venture.

Upped to 2m for a handicap win at York Ebor meeting (good to firm) last August; tried front-running to positive effect against her own sex over about 1m6f on her subsequent two starts when winning the Group 2 Park Hill at Doncaster (good to soft) and second in Group 1 at Longchamp (very soft); has a form chance on this return but the stayer's mantle will have to be shed.
horses.breeding: b m Golden Horn - Livia's Dream

horses.spotlight_comment: Peak efforts were as a 3yo but reappearance at Meydan this January saw his first win since 2023; nearly won another 1m6f Group 3 there next time, before a headstrong display (set up big lead) saw him tail off in 2m Dubai Gold Cup five weeks ago; the latter was in blinkers (first time since September) which are unsurprisingly left off today; thereabouts if bouncing back.

4.05.betting_forecast: 2/1 Golden Redemption, 11/4 Elarak, 7/1 Shah, 8/1 Leadman, 10/1 Benacre, Billyjoh, Silver Ghost, 14/1 Misunderstood.
4.05.spotlight_verdict: Class act ELARAK (nap) was a convincing winner over C&D last September and he can defy top weight on his second start of the season. The admirably consistent Golden Redemption could be a big danger, however, while Shah was a promising 2yo in 2024 and is fascinating contender on this first outing since.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: Close third from the front at Musselburgh (7f, good) on April 12 and didn't lead when drawn wide and fifth of 11 there (7f, good) last Sunday; could give a good account if usual prominent tactics are applied but there's a suspicion he's vulnerable up in grade.
horses.breeding: b g Australia - Sent From Heaven

horses.spotlight_comment: Made it 3-6 when winning a C&D handicap (good to firm) last September, making virtually all; gelded subsequently; reappeared with close fourth of eight in conditions race at Thirsk (7f, good) three weeks ago and could show the benefit of that outing today; this 4yo is firmly in calculations.

Placed on all four handicap starts last year (7f/6f, good to firm/good), on the final occasion keeping on for 1l third here when the drop back to 6f looked against him; returned with solid third at Kempton (7f, AW) in March; major player for trainer who has won two of the last four runnings.
horses.breeding: b c Medaglia d'Oro - Redemption Day

horses.spotlight_comment: He has a modest strike-rate for one of his ability (2-19) and needs everything to drop right; however, he's well treated on last year's best efforts and may have needed his recent reappearance run at Thirsk; not ruled out.

Won 1m 2yo Group 3 at Longchamp in 2024; reappeared with good third in Group 3 there last April; form went the wrong way subsequently and he changed hands for 37,000euros last November; gelded since; however, his new yard does extremely well with French recruits and this 4yo has an attractive mark to work with if tapping back into his historic promise; watch the betting.

Runner-up in 2024 on first three 2yo starts (7f/1m, good to firm/good to soft) before easily making all in 7f AW novice; off since, with gelding/wind ops in the meantime; it's a hefty absence to defy but he has potential off his opening mark if retaining his ability; the betting will be interesting.
horses.breeding: b g Sea The Stars - Shahah

horses.spotlight_comment: Won over C&D (good) last May on her second start of last season and followed up at Goodwood (7f, good) later that month; she failed to kick on subsequently but perhaps a break will have helped and she's not discounted on her reappearance.
horses.breeding: gr f Phoenix Of Spain - Kykuit

4.40.betting_forecast: 11/8 Cerro Blanco, 2/1 Stellar Sunrise, 7/2 Saber Strike, 10/1 Jel Pepper, 16/1 Ellusive Butterfly, 33/1 Maximized.
4.40.spotlight_verdict: Having impressed in a handicap at Newbury on his recent reappearance, STELLAR SUNRISE is selected to continue his rise through the ranks and take this Listed prize. Godolphin colt Cerro Blanco was a warm order when winning a C&D maiden on his recent debut and could be a big danger, however, while Saber Strike is another exciting prospect who is 1-1.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: Sent off the 4-9 favourite when winning on debut over C&D (good) 17 days ago; his dam was a Listed winner and he's entered in the St James's Palace Stakes; could have lots more to offer for leading stable; strong claims.

7f AW maiden winner who was fourth of 14 in the Group 3 Fred Darling at Newbury (7f, good) a fortnight ago; she's raced five times and others may have greater potential, while she could do with settling better, but she appears to be improving and might not be far away.

Front-runner who had nearly 2l to spare when winning 26-runner sales race over C&D (good); held in fourth of seven on reappearance in Listed race at Newcastle (1m, AW) but could benefit from that run and the drop back in trip; no surprise to see a bold bid back on the Rowley Mile.
horses.breeding: b g Inns Of Court - Kasalla

horses.spotlight_comment: Won his first two starts last May/June then fifth in a pair of Group 2 races; twice placed at Meydan early this year but beaten about 6l when third of five in conditions race over this C&D (good) recently and Cerro Blanco may well be the yard's chief hope under Billy Loughnane.

230,000gns yearling who was backed into 5-2 when readily making a winning debut at Redcar (6f, good) last November; he's entered in the 6f Group 1 Commonwealth Cup but there's every chance he'll be suited by 7f and this highly likeable prospect is in good hands to progress; one to consider.

Won in good style in a big field on nursery debut at York (7f, good to firm) last August and soft ground may not have suited in the Group 3 Horris Hill at Newbury in October; returned with commanding handicap win at Newbury (7f, good) a fortnight ago and holds leading form claims.

5.15.betting_forecast: 4/1 Lady Roxby, 6/1 Angel Love, Paradise Walk, 7/1 Lightning Polka, 8/1 Cuban Lady, Lady Kodiac, 10/1 Powdering, 12/1
5.15.spotlight_verdict: The 3yo LIGHTNING POLKA reappears with the Ed Walker yard in fine form and she's taken to tap back into the notable promise shown when making a winning debut last September. The lightly raced 4yo Cuban Lady showed some solid form last season and is second choice with Oisin Murphy up for her reappearance, with the 3yo handicap newcomer Angel Love next on the list. Lady Roxby and Lady Kodiac are other interesting contenders.[Ben Hutton]

horses.spotlight_comment: She ran 11 times last year and won twice, including Listed race at Ripon last August (6f, good; modest form for the grade); reappeared with 2l fourth of seven against males in handicap at Pontefract (6f, good) ten days ago and she has an each-way chance if building on that.

Three wins last year and campaign concluded with good fourth of 11 over this C&D (good); down the field on reappearance at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) in March but may have needed the run and is not ruled out.

Not seen to best effect last October on final 3yo start but she'd previous gone close twice in a row, on the first occasion on the other Newmarket course (6f, good to firm); reappears with Oisin Murphy booked and this lightly raced filly may have more to offer this season; possible contender.
horses.breeding: br f Havana Grey - Lady Lynetta

horses.spotlight_comment: 4yo who won last summer on her first two starts (6f/7f, AW); four lesser runs followed last year (turf/AW), however, and there was no return to form on her recent reappearance at Southwell (6f, AW).

Built upon last August's promising debut at Ripon (5f, good to firm) to post two novice wins at Chelmsford (6f, AW) in the autumn; only fifth of seven in conditions race at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) three weeks ago but may have needed that comeback run and she retains potential on handicap debut.

Progressive last year, a campaign that culminated with a neck second of 11 over C&D (good); reappeared with solid third at Kempton (6f, AW) 25 days ago and could build on that effort today; respected.
horses.breeding: b f King Of Change - M'selle

horses.spotlight_comment: Looked good when winning on debut at Haydock (6f, good) last September; didn't kick on subsequently and came third of four on handicap debut at Lingfield (6f, AW) in November last time, but maybe a break will have helped this half-sister to 6f Group 3 winner Light Refrain; yard in fine form.
horses.breeding: ch f Night Of Thunder - Light Music

horses.spotlight_comment: Down the field at Kempton (6f, AW) 25 days ago but she was back from an absence and had a wide trip; close third on the other Newmarket course (6f, good to firm) last June on her final outing of last year, when tackling a sprint trip for the first time, and she's not written off.

Made it 2-3 on AW when winning on handicap/seasonal debut at Wolverhampton (6f, AW) last April; then off until the autumn, when running some respectable races on turf; has to better that form to win off her current mark but this 4yo remains lightly raced and is not discounted.

Runner-up on all three starts (7f/6f, AW), most recently at Wolverhampton in March following an 82-day break; improvement is needed off her opening mark but there's potential in her pedigree and she's in the right hands to progress; wears first-time blinkers.

Inconsistent on AW this year but she was short-headed at Lingfield (7f) in February and denied a clear run when third at Southwell (6f) last time; has won here and she might not be far away if she's on a going day.

Won Newbury novice (6f, good) last August on third start and followed up in three-runner nursery at Goodwood (6f, heavy); faced some tough tasks subsequently and she reverts to a handicap for her reappearance in a race her trainer won last year; this 3yo could give a good account.
